title: Hosted API traffic steering (GSLB + DNS)
author: Dev Patel
body:
> **Archived 2024-06-18:** this page is superseded by "Global traffic routing controls (GSLB + DNS): Hosted API" and is kept for reference only.

h1. Purpose
How to move production Hosted API traffic between regions with Redwood's Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB) and DNS controls. Use it for outages, planned maintenance and game days.

*Entry point:* api.redwoodinference.com
*Owned by:* Eng Infra

h1. Routing architecture (summary)
- api.redwoodinference.com resolves to a GSLB endpoint.
- GSLB spreads traffic across regional gateways by weighted targets.
- Each regional gateway hands requests to the regional routing service, which picks model backends in that region.

h1. Regions and failover pairings
Primary -> secondary pairs:
- us-east-1 -> us-west-2
- eu-west-1 -> eu-west-2
- ap-southeast-1 -> ap-northeast-1

h1. Changing weights
Weights live in Terraform-backed config, but during incidents use the "trafficctl" emergency tool rather than waiting on an IaC cycle.

*Tool:* trafficctl
*Auth:* requires oncall elevated role "infra-oncall-admin"

h2. Check current distribution
- trafficctl gslb get --record api.redwoodinference.com

Typical output:
- us-east-1-gw weight=100
- us-west-2-gw weight=0

h2. Weighted failover (preferred)
1) Lower TTL temporarily
- trafficctl dns set-ttl --record api.redwoodinference.com --ttl 30
2) Move 10% to secondary
- trafficctl gslb set-weights --record api.redwoodinference.com --weights us-east-1-gw=90,us-west-2-gw=10
3) Watch metrics for 5-10 minutes
4) Move to 50/50
- trafficctl gslb set-weights --record api.redwoodinference.com --weights us-east-1-gw=50,us-west-2-gw=50
5) Watch metrics for 5-10 minutes
6) Move 100% to secondary
- trafficctl gslb set-weights --record api.redwoodinference.com --weights us-east-1-gw=0,us-west-2-gw=100
7) Leave the low TTL in place for the first hour after cutover, then restore the steady-state TTL
- trafficctl dns set-ttl --record api.redwoodinference.com --ttl 600

h2. Hard failover (primary down)
When the primary region is completely down (no metrics, no gateway health):
- trafficctl dns set-ttl --record api.redwoodinference.com --ttl 30
- trafficctl gslb set-weights --record api.redwoodinference.com --weights us-east-1-gw=0,us-west-2-gw=100

h1. Rollback
Restore the previous weights recorded in the incident log. Steady state is 100/0 to the designated primary.
- trafficctl gslb set-weights --record api.redwoodinference.com --weights us-east-1-gw=100,us-west-2-gw=0
- trafficctl dns set-ttl --record api.redwoodinference.com --ttl 600

h1. Validation signals (per region)
- gateway_5xx_rate{region}
- gateway_request_latency_p95{region}
- router_queue_depth{region}
- runtime_gpu_utilization{region}
- client_stream_disconnect_rate{region}

h1. Safety notes
- TTL changes only reach new resolver lookups; cached client entries may linger.
- Paste every trafficctl command you run into the incident channel and the postmortem.
- Do not flip weights more often than every 5 minutes unless the service is melting.
- This page is retained for history only; follow the current Global traffic routing controls page.
